build_patterns.name: Micro-model Meshes
evidence: Speculative decoding uses a cheap draft model to generate candidate tokens that are verified in parallel by a target model.
SD reduces the latency or increases the throughput of decoding by the factor where a round of speculation is the generation and subsequent verification of each block of draft tokens

We train NSA models in which a block of tokens attend to the same subset of the context in the “token selection” attention path. We show that these models have the same language modeling quality as baseline NSA models, while achieving up to 3.5× higher operational intensity during the verification step of speculative decoding.
build_patterns.description: MatX uses speculative decoding which explicitly employs multiple models (a lightweight draft model and a heavier target model) working together to accelerate decoding. This is an ensemble/mesh pattern where work is split across cheaper and more expensive models with coordinated verification.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Block-quantized attention with MXFP4 and causal-leakage fix
evidence: Quantizing attention improves efficiency on two fronts: the model has higher compute throughput, and loads fewer bytes per key/value.
We present a fix that enables training with MXFP4 in both attention and the attention gradient.

Leakage only occurs when the -th block-diagonal tile of is multiplied with the -th quantized block of . So we can prevent future leakage by using unquantized and when multiplying the -th tile of with the -th block of , while using block quantized matrix multiplications everywhere else.
Quantized ops | matrix multiplies in attention + matrix multiplies in attention gradient
Forwards pass rounding | Round-to-Nearest | Backwards pass rounding | Stochastic Rounding
discovered_patterns.description: They convert attention Q/K/V matrix multiplies to block-quantized formats (MXFP4) for throughput and lower memory traffic, but discovered a causal leakage path when quantization blocks span token positions. Their solution: selectively execute the particular block-diagonal tile multiplications (where a query's block and a value's block align) using unquantized (full-precision) operands while keeping block-quantized matmuls elsewhere. They also quantize attention gradients and control forward/backward rounding (R2N forward, stochastic rounding backward).
discovered_patterns.why_notable: This is a concrete, surgical mitigation of a subtle correctness issue introduced by block quantization, enabling end-to-end training with attention quantized (including gradients). It combines low-level numeric choices (stochastic rounding) with algorithmic selective dequantization — uncommon in standard quantization work.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Decoupled K/V heads (Multi Value Attention, MVA) and Sparse V
evidence: We decouple the number of K heads from the number of V heads
Typically, we set the number of K heads to 1 and the number of V heads equal to the number of Q heads.
We propose Sparse Multi Value Attention (SMVA): use one K head, as many V heads as possible (equal to the number of Q heads), and access the V heads sparsely.
Sparse V loads only the most important values, while MVA decreases the number of K heads
discovered_patterns.description: They change attention head topology: fewer/dense K heads (often 1) and many V heads. Then they sparsify the retrieval of V entries from the KV cache by thresholding attention probabilities, loading only values above a fixed probability threshold. This both reduces KV cache bandwidth and preserves quality when sparsity is introduced during training.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Decoupling K and V head counts is a practical, quantifiable tradeoff between memory bandwidth and quality; combining it with training-time sparsity (threshold-based) to achieve large sparsity ratios is uncommon and impactful for inference bandwidth-limited deployments.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Training-time thresholded Sparse V instead of post-training top-k
evidence: We introduce V-sparsity during training, rather than after training. We find this allows us to achieve 4x greater sparsity at the same quality levels.
Rather than inducing sparsity via a top-k computation, we induce it by comparing the attention probabilities to a fixed threshold.
We found that enabling sparsity upon reaching 60% of the training steps works best
discovered_patterns.description: Instead of applying top-k sparsification post-hoc (which requires expensive sorting/top-k in inference), they begin applying a fixed-probability threshold during training (enabled at a late training phase, e.g., 60% steps). At inference they set probabilities below threshold to zero. This allows higher sparsity for a given quality level and removes expensive top-k selection.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Shifting sparsification into training and using a cheap threshold makes sparse V practical and efficient, avoids top-k costs, and achieves much higher sparsity for same quality — a practical systems+training co-design.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Speculative Decoding + Blockwise Sparse Attention alignment (force block-level shared context)
evidence: Speculative decoding (SD) and blockwise sparse attention both accelerate LLM decoding, but when combined naively, the KV cache may lose sparsity during the verification step of SD.
We show that forcing all draft tokens to attend to the same subset of the context restores sparsity while preserving model quality.

To always achieve the best case operational intensity during verification, we replace with , where are the keys and values selected by token . During training, for each which is a multiple of , is reused by the tokens following token .
discovered_patterns.description: When combining speculative decoding with blockwise sparse attention, they enforce that a block of draft tokens all attend to the same subset of context blocks (token-selection path reuses the same selection for the block). This preserves KV-cache block sparsity during the parallel verification step, substantially improving operational intensity for verification.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: This is a systems-aware modification to attention behavior to maintain hardware-efficient sparsity across a two-model pipeline (draft+verify), enabling large practical speedups when combining two techniques that otherwise interfere.

discovered_patterns.why_notable: Using JAX and TPUs for reproducible research is common, but the focused seqax codebase containing these attention variants and ablations adds practical value for replication.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Practical ablation-driven validation of attention variants (MHA/GQA/MQA/MVA/SMVA)
evidence: We compared different attention mechanisms in the table below. For each model, we report the loss, FLOPs, and KV cache requirements, all relative to MHA.
SMVA (with 8 Q heads) achieved the lowest amount of FLOPs needed for the forward pass, reduced the KV cache size by half compared to MHA, and had the smallest KV cache bandwidth requirements.

discovered_patterns.why_notable: The holistic metric (FLOP-equivalent cost combining KV fetch and compute) and rigorous control of randomness make their comparisons operationally meaningful for inference-oriented architecture choices.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Introduce sparsity during training and long-duration prefill-focused training
evidence: We find that enabling sparsity upon reaching 60% of the training steps works best
We trained the model for 150,000 steps (9.8B tokens, batch 32, sequence length 2048), approximately five times the number of tokens suggested by the Chinchilla scaling laws
To minimize noise in our experiments, all experiments visit the training data in the same random order, and all models are initialized using the same random seed.
discovered_patterns.description: They adopt training schedules that emphasize inference quality (longer training than Chinchilla recommendations), introduce sparsity late in training, and use deterministic/reproducible experiment protocols (same seed, same data order) for low-variance measurement.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Prioritizing longer training to optimize inference and adding architectural sparsity during training is a clear shift from training-to-optimize-FLOPs toward inference-aware model design.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Emphasis on low-precision compute and roofline-based FLOP-equivalent inference cost modeling

we also compute a FLOP-equivalent cost with a roofline model that estimates the decoding cost as the maximum of the KV cache fetch time and computation time.
This disconnect has led to models with ~70% efficiency during training but only ~10% efficiency during inference.
discovered_patterns.description: MatX ties model-level architectural changes to hardware metrics: they measure inference 'FLOP-equivalent cost' using a roofline model that considers KV cache fetches and computation, emphasizing low-precision formats and memory bandwidth optimizations aligned with hardware capabilities.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: The explicit, quantitative roofline framing combined with low-precision numeric engineering and selective algorithm changes demonstrates true hardware/software co-design rather than isolated model tweaks.

discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Two-model pipeline (Speculative Decoding: draft + target) with attention-level co-design
evidence: Speculative decoding uses a cheap draft model to generate candidate tokens that are verified in parallel by a target model.
forcing all draft tokens to attend to the same subset of the context restores sparsity while preserving model quality.
discovered_patterns.description: They treat speculative decoding as a two-model system (draft and target) and modify the attention behavior of target/draft (forcing block-level shared attention selection) so that KV cache sparsity is preserved during the verification step, maximizing combined throughput.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Rather than viewing speculative decoding and sparse attention as orthogonal, they co-design the attention selection mechanism to make both techniques synergistic — a practical orchestration pattern at the model-attention level.

novel_approaches.why_novel: Pinpoints a subtle correctness failure mode introduced by block quantization across token positions and proposes an efficient selective dequantization strategy rather than abandoning block quantization entirely.
novel_approaches.potential_impact: Enables training (including backward pass) with block quantized attention formats (MXFP4) at scale without harming causal language-modeling correctness — unlocking higher throughput and lower memory traffic in both training and inference.

novel_approaches.approach: Introduce Sparse V via a fixed probability threshold during training (late-stage enablement) instead of post-training top-k

novel_approaches.potential_impact: Significantly reduces KV-cache bandwidth requirements for inference, enabling up to ~8x KV bandwidth savings in some configurations while maintaining quality.

novel_approaches.approach: Decoupling K and V head counts (MVA) and combining with Sparse V to form SMVA

novel_approaches.potential_impact: Preserves model quality while drastically lowering KV cache size and fetch bandwidth, reducing inference bottlenecks in long-context models.

novel_approaches.approach: Force blockwise draft tokens to attend to the same subset of context for compatibility between NSA block sparsity and speculative decoding

novel_approaches.potential_impact: Enables higher operational intensity and larger end-to-end speedups for decoding with long contexts when using SD + block-sparse attention.

unique_findings: They discovered a subtle causal leak introduced by block-wise quantization: the per-block shared scale (used in microscaling/MXFP4) makes quantized K/V at earlier token positions depend on later tokens inside the same quantization block, which breaks causal LM training.

Their surgical fix: keep the specific block-diagonal tile multiply (the tile where query-block index == key-block index) unquantized while using block-quantized matmuls everywhere else. This preserves throughput for most ops but blocks the single leakage path.

They quantize not only forward attention matmuls but also the attention gradient, and use different rounding strategies: round-to-nearest for forward, stochastic rounding for backward—an explicit rounding-mode design to stabilize low-precision training.

Novel experimental sanity check: compare parallel prefill loss vs autoregressive (one-token-at-a-time) loss to detect future leakage from quantization. The gap served as an operational signal for leakage.
They decouple K and V head counts (Multi Value Attention, MVA): use one or few K heads but many V heads. This recognizes that V heads drive quality while K heads dominate KV cache bandwidth.

Sparse V: induce sparsity by thresholding normalized attention probabilities (fixed threshold) rather than top-k, and—critically—turn on sparsity during training (best at ~60% through training). This yields much higher usable sparsity at a given quality than post-training top-k.

Combining MVA + Sparse V -> SMVA: one dense K head, many sparsely accessed V heads. This attains near-GQA/MHA quality while reducing KV cache size and bandwidth dramatically; they present a FLOP-equivalent roofline evaluation.

Speculative decoding + blockwise sparse attention interaction: they force blocks of draft tokens to attend to the same subset of KV blocks (via mask/design) so that verification keeps blockwise sparsity and thus high operational intensity—restoring up to ~3.5× verification speedup.

Practical trade: Sparse V and thresholding require fully normalized softmax probabilities (so incompatible with online/fused softmax kernels like FlashAttention) and defeat lockstep K/V prefetching; they accept losing K/V fusion for larger bandwidth wins.

Engineering nuance: to simulate/implement sparse V they sometimes fetch V densely then multiply by sparse probs, trading memory access patterns vs. algorithmic simplicity; the whole stack requires changes across attention kernels, KV-cache fetch, and decoding verification.

story_angles.headline: Cut KV bandwidth by up to 8x: How Sparse Multi Value Attention (SMVA) buys real inference savings
story_angles.summary: MatX combines Multi Value Attention with a training-time Sparse V threshold to deliver near-MHA quality while slashing KV cache size and fetch bandwidth. Their results claim up to 8x memory-bandwidth reduction and lower FLOP-equivalent costs, making this a pragmatic path to cheaper, higher-throughput decoding.
evidence: SMVA (one K head, many V heads, sparse V) achieved quality on par with Grouped Query Attention while reducing KV bandwidth by up to a factor of 8 for common architectures.
Experiments show SMVA with 8 Q heads reduced KV cache size to 56% of MHA and KV fetch to ~11% yielding the smallest FLOP-equivalent cost in parameter-controlled comparisons.

story_angles.headline: Fixing causal leakage in block-quantized attention: the MXFP4 training trick every low-precision team should know
story_angles.summary: Block quantization of attention scales can let future tokens leak into earlier logits via shared block scales. MatX proposes selectively unquantizing the block-diagonal tile during attention-to-value multiplies to preserve causality and validates it with a controlled Leaky vs Fixed 1B-model experiment.
evidence: Block quantization shares a scale per block so a later token outlier can change the scale and influence earlier positions, breaking causal modeling.

Validation: 'Leaky' model (fully quantized) showed a +0.10 gap between parallel and autoregressive loss while the 'Fixed' model (selective unquantize) had no gap; grad-norms behaved pathologically for the Leaky model.

story_angles.headline: Train sparsity, don't graft it on later: why MatX abandons post-training top-k for thresholded Sparse V during training
story_angles.summary: Contrary to common post-hoc sparsification (top-k), MatX injects Sparse V during training using a fixed probability threshold and a schedule. They report up to 4x higher sparsity at the same quality, and claim thresholding is cheaper and more hardware-friendly than top-k.
evidence: Applying top-k sparsification post-training increased loss by ~1.5% in reproductions, whereas enabling sparsity during training matched MHA loss within 0.2% with much higher sparsity.
Threshold-based sparsity avoids expensive sorting/top-k and enables replacing top-k with a cheap comparison, and the team found activating sparsity around 60% of training steps works best.

story_angles.headline: Hardware-aware model design: how MatX’s chip-to-model co-design shapes attention primitives
story_angles.summary: MatX presents a coherent story of designing attention mechanisms (MXFP4 quant formats, block-quantization fixes, SMVA) with direct awareness of accelerator primitives and memory-bandwidth constraints. This is a playbook for teams building model+hardware stacks rather than model-only research.
evidence: MatX emphasizes block-quantized matrix multiplications required by modern accelerators and designs fixes to preserve causal modeling while using microscaling formats (MXFP4).
Their experiments are run on Cloud TPUs and they explicitly use a roofline model comparing KV fetch time vs compute to compute FLOP-equivalent cost, signaling hardware-aware evaluation.

These are easy for platform incumbents or open-source projects to integrate without needing MatX as a full product.

The seqax codebase and JAX/TPU experiments imply reproducible research artifacts that others could adopt.

The methods build on well-known primitives (MHA, GQA, MQA) and use software-level interventions (block quantization policy, thresholded sparsity) which competitors with teams of engineers could implement.

competitive_analysis.moat_explanation: MatX’s moat arises from combined hardware + algorithm expertise, proprietary low-precision formats, and validated training techniques that require co-designed support. This is non-trivial to replicate and provides advantage for inference-heavy LLM deployments. However, large incumbents (NVIDIA, Google, Intel) possess vast engineering resources, established ecosystems, and market share; they can adopt similar low-precision instructions, integrate comparable compiler support, or buy/start similar research efforts. Thus the moat is meaningful but not impregnable — defensibility depends on execution speed, IP protections (designs, compiler/tooling), customer wins, and continued research/benchmarks proving superior TCO on real workloads.

evidence_quotes: Quantizing attention improves efficiency on two fronts: the model has higher compute throughput, and loads fewer bytes per key/value.
training with MXFP4 in both attention and the attention gradient
We trained a pair of 1B-parameter models on the C4 dataset, with MXFP4 for attention and the attention gradient.
The Fixed model remained well behaved throughout training. However, the Leaky model had training dynamics associated with future leakage.
During experiments, we compared attention mechanisms such as GQA, MQA, MVA, SMVA and MHA, with specific references to their FLOPs, KV cache requirements, and losses.
We trained 101 million parameter model using the seqax codebase with various attention variants.
Speculative decoding (SD) and blockwise sparse attention are discussed as techniques to accelerate LLM decoding.
The content centers on methods to accelerate and improve generation in transformer-based models (LLMs) through quantization, sparsity, and alternative attention mechanisms.

Block-quantized attention leakage mitigation: selectively perform unquantized multiplies for the block-diagonal tile of K×V (the tile where query and value positions share the same quantization block index) while using block-quantized matmuls everywhere else to prevent future-token leakage in causal LM training.

Training-aware quantized attention and gradients: apply MXFP4 to both attention forward and attention gradient paths, with mixed rounding strategies (forward: Round-to-Nearest; backward: Stochastic Rounding) and a maxabs calibration scale-selection.

Exploiting quantization scale behavior as side-channel: identifying and diagnosing how block-level scale selection (e.g., influenced by outliers at block end) can encode future information and cause causality leaks.

Sparse Multi Value Attention (SMVA): decouple number of Key heads and Value heads (e.g., one K head, many V heads) to combine MQA-like KV cache savings with many (sparsely-accessed) V heads for quality.

Threshold-based Sparse V applied during training (not post-training): induce sparsity by zeroing attention probabilities below a fixed threshold and enabling sparsity partway through training (e.g., ~60% of steps) to reach much higher sparsity at similar quality than post-training top-k.
Replace top-k with probability-threshold sparsification: cheaper threshold computation that preserves quality and enables efficient training-time sparsity.
GCD-based head partitioning for arbitrary K/V ratios: reshape/partition heads to support non-integer decoupling of K and V heads.

Enforce blockwise uniform KV selection for speculative decoding: force all draft tokens in a block to attend to the same subset of context blocks (via mask/training-time reuse) to preserve KV cache sparsity during verification and dramatically increase operational intensity.
Demonstrated incompatibility analysis with fused K/V implementations (e.g., Flash Attention) and practical tradeoffs between K/V fusion and memory-bandwidth savings from Sparse V.
